review_note: COVID logistics and supply-chain constraints were manageable rather than intervention pressure. Revenue rose 14%, adjusted operating profit 31%, EBITA margin recovered to 25%, cash conversion reached 104%, adjusted net debt fell from £5.7m to £1.4m and the order book reached a record 23 weeks, supplying exceptional quantified contrary evidence.

Inflation, isolated smaller-business recovery issues and acquisition-related debt were contained. Revenue rose 20%, adjusted operating profit 16%, Organic EBITA margin held at 25%, cash conversion improved to 90%, adjusted net debt declined and the 16.2-week order book remained healthy, supplying multiple strong quantified contrary indicators.

A challenging environment and ongoing footprint and restructuring savings programme supplied contained pressure, but the programme was substantially complete and its disclosed closures are excluded as future target events. Sales rose 5%, underlying operating profit 8%, underlying margin was broadly stable at 13.4%, and strong execution across sectors supplied multiple quantified contrary indicators.

Macroeconomic headwinds, inflation, lower volumes and metals prices accompanied a 21% Group underlying operating-profit decline, sharp Clean Air margin deterioration, £41m of major impairment and restructuring charges, and a wide-ranging operating-model transformation targeting substantial cost savings. Free cash flow remained positive at £74m, leverage was 1.6x, second-half margins improved and cumulative Clean Air cash generation was strong, providing meaningful contrary evidence. The disclosed transformation is excluded as a future target event.
